sources.title: American Museum of Natural History: Coast Salish
sources.note: Direct original, community-curated introduction and Seattle/Vancouver sections. Independent Nations and related distinct languages; no unitary Coast Salish state.

sources.title: Suquamish Tribe: History and Culture
sources.note: Direct official history. Winter houses, seasonal camps, 1855 treaty, Old Man House destruction and boarding schools. Avoids competing estimates of longhouse length.

sources.title: Burke Museum: Rare woolly dog hair found in Coast Salish blanket (2017)
sources.note: Direct original, blanket 2.5E1965, exposed warp and testing; maker and original owners unrecorded. Does not repeat the article’s oversimplified explanation of dog disappearance.

sources.title: Burke Museum: Spinning and Processing, Woven in Wool
sources.note: Direct accessible exhibit text. Spindle construction and diatomaceous earth cleaning. Contemporary exhibit description, not a precisely dated ancient recipe.

sources.title: Jesse Morin, Thomas C. A. Royle and colleagues: Sex-selective salmon harvesting (2021)
sources.note: Direct full primary article, abstract, results and discussion. Two of four sites show male-biased chum remains; motive for selection explicitly not certain. Uses broad precontact dating because discussion/conclusion calibrated ranges differ slightly.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Restoring Salish sea gardens, 2018 to 2023 report
sources.note: Direct original report and video transcript. Hul’q’umi’num’ and WSÁNEĆ collaboration, wall and beach maintenance; distinguishes completed work from older targets.

sources.title: Jordan Wilson: Teachings of the Community, Musqueam Teaching Kit
sources.note: Direct primary PDF, chapter 2, page 1, first-person account of 2012 vigil lasting over 200 days. No generic claims about all Coast Salish communities.

sources.title: Squamish Nation: Our History
sources.note: Direct official chronology. July 23, 1923 amalgamation of sixteen bands; public prose does not confuse that government reorganization with origin of the people.

sources.title: Northwest Indian Fisheries Commission: Understanding Tribal Treaty Rights
sources.note: Direct original commission pamphlet, printed page 3: February 12, 1974, half harvestable salmon and co-management. Historical finding, not legal advice.

sources.title: Tulalip Lushootseed Department: Greeting Phrases
sources.note: Direct original modern community language resource. Exact short witness haʔɬ dadatu təkʷtəkʷəlus / Good morning owl. Original Latin-based spelling retained; no ancient inscription claimed.

sources.title: Tulalip News: Lushootseed at Marysville Pilchuck, September 14, 2019
sources.note: Indexed original tribal newspaper article, relevant paragraphs about two full classes, daily routines, feelings, weather and archived elder recordings.

sources.title: American Museum of Natural History: Tsimshian
sources.note: Direct community-curated original, consulting curator David Boxley; language audio credited to First Voices/Ts’msyen Sm’algya̱x Language Authority, text thanks Sarah Booth and Haayk Foundation. Introduction, clans, potlatches and exact greeting.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Metlakatla Pass National Historic Site
sources.note: Direct designation record: Pike Island archaeology, pre/postcontact villages, Metlakatla relocation sequence. Distinguishes island’s five sites from 46 around the wider pass.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Kitselas Canyon National Historic Site
sources.note: Direct original, five village sites, fortified Gitlaxdzok and nineteenth-century trade gateway. Does not repeat claim of unique fortification on whole north coast.

sources.title: Lax Kw’alaams Band: History
sources.note: Direct official history of Nine Tribes, Legex trade fees, Fort Simpson 1834, wage work and colonial change. Excludes suspect 650 houses by 1880 statistic and conflicting missionary arrival date.

sources.title: Gitga’at Nation: Spring Harvest Tradition at Kiel Camp (2024)
sources.note: Direct original dated April 30, 2024. Kiel on Princess Royal Island; red laver, halibut processing, seasonal trade and storage. Modern community account with historical practices explicitly signaled.

sources.title: Gitga’at Nation: Fall Harvest, Words to Know (2023)
sources.note: Direct original dated August 28, 2023. Describes northern riceroot, foods, grease trade and dayks dessert. Used only for named contemporary Gitga’at description, not a precontact sugar recipe.

sources.title: Gitxaała Nation: Lach Klan School
sources.note: Direct indexed original, K4 to 12 school with on-the-land education, language, breakfast/snack and fruit/vegetable programs; not a claim of unchanged historical curricula.

sources.title: Metlakatla First Nation: Cultural Heritage
sources.note: Direct original, oral history interviews, community mapping and GIS; heritage and archaeological monitoring. This is Canadian Metlakatla, distinct from Alaska community.

sources.title: Metlakatla Indian Community: Constitution and By-laws, ratified 1944
sources.note: Direct primary document reprinted 1946, Oklahoma law-school transcription. Preamble 1891 reserve; Article III council; Article IV section 7 and By-laws Article II section 6 public health; December 19 ratification. Historical rules only.

sources.title: Metlakatla Indian Community: Community and government
sources.note: Direct official homepage. Contemporary Alaska tribal government and economy; does not repeat misleading shorthand that reserve itself began with 1944 constitution.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Regional cultural and linguistic grouping; not a unitary polity and not Interior Salish generally.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: Decoded world-1492.json MultiPolygon bbox [-126.3667,46.4050,-121.2006,51.1275], broad coastal BC/Washington region. Index 1492 to 1500 is map coverage only. No alias absorption.
batchIdentityNotes.publicQualification: Opening explicitly identifies independent Nations and approximate broad outline; every concrete local practice names its community.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Tsimshian regional peoples and historically specific communities; excludes separate Gitxsan and Nisg̱a’a identities.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: Decoded world-1492.json MultiPolygon bbox [-130.2979,52.6496,-127.5547,55.9579], northern BC outline. It omits later Annette Island community and cannot express all local territories. Index 1492 to 1500 is coverage.
batchIdentityNotes.publicQualification: Opening says partial homeland and distinguishes neighbors. Canadian and Alaska Metlakatla are explicitly separated; 1887 migration not made universal.
